narrator.instruct: Gripping, excited storyteller telling an astonishing true space story, brisk and punchy, never calm.

young.instruct: A playful, cocky astronaut on the Moon showing off over the radio, grinning, a little breathless.

duke.instruct: An astronaut tipping over backward in panic, startled and breathless, urgent.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On the Moon, a jump of just four feet nearly killed a man, and his own backpack did it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: April nineteen seventy-two. Apollo sixteen's Charlie Duke and John Young finish their last moonwalk.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Munich's Olympics are coming, so they invent the Moon Olympics.

lines.speaker: young
lines.text: Watch this, Charlie. I can jump flat-footed, straight up!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Up here, you weigh one sixth as much. Young bounces like a kid.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Duke wants to beat him. He makes a big push and flies about four feet high.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But as he straightens up, his backpack pulls him over backward.

lines.speaker: duke
lines.text: Whoa, whoa, I can't correct it!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He falls four feet, right onto the backpack. And that backpack is his air.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You see, the Moon cuts your weight, but not your mass.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Duke said the pack weighed as much as he did. Once it tips, it keeps going.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And it's a fiberglass shell. Crack it, and your air rushes out.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Young helps him up. Duke freezes, listening for a hiss, a leak, anything.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Now picture you, jumping twice as high, flipping right over.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That's why moonwalkers loped and skipped, and hopped only for fun.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So on the Moon, keep your jumps small. Remember the man who didn't.
